description: Rutherfordium is a synthetic chemical element with symbol Rf and atomic number 104, named after physicist Ernest Rutherford. It is not found in nature and can only be made in a particle accelerator. It is a radioactive d-block element in period 7 and group 4, behaving as the heavier homolog to hafnium.
characteristics: The most stable known isotope, 267Rf, has a half-life of about 48 minutes. Rutherfordium is expected to form a very stable, refractory oxide (RfO2) and reacts with halogens to form volatile tetrahalides (RfX4). It exhibits a stable +4 oxidation state and is expected to form a less stable +3 state, with chemical properties resembling other group 4 elements rather than lead.
